writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 183 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Nowadays more and more people keep learning new skills to adapt to a fast-changing world. This trend, in my view, is not a passing fashion but a wise and even necessary response to the age we live in.
The most obvious reason lies in the speed of technological change. Skills that guaranteed a stable job ten years ago may become outdated overnight, so those who stop learning risk being replaced. Take my cousin as an example. As a traditional accountant, she felt threatened when her company introduced financial software, yet instead of complaining she spent her evenings mastering data analysis. Within a year she was promoted rather than laid off. Her experience convinces me that continuous learning is what keeps a person competitive. Beyond the workplace, learning also enriches our daily life and broadens our horizons.
In conclusion, keeping pace with a changing world through lifelong learning is no longer optional but essential. Rather than fearing change, we should treat every new skill as a bridge to a wider future. I firmly believe that whoever embraces new skills today will stand firm tomorrow.

cloze.title: 2022年6月·第2套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: Thinking kind thoughts about yourself and your loved ones can prove beneficial for your overall wellbeing, empirical evidence has shown. Researchers carried out an investigation to explore the __(26)__ between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state.
passages.zh: 实证研究表明，对自己和所爱之人怀有善意的想法被证明对个人的整体健康有益。研究人员开展了一项调查，以探究怀有善意想法与个人心理状态之间的相关性。

passages.en: For the study, five groups of participants were presented with a different set of audio instructions, some of which encouraged the participants to think __(27)__ about themselves and others which persuaded them to think in a self-critical manner. After listening to the audio instructions, the participants were asked to answer a series of questions. These included whether they felt agitated, how likely they were to show kindness to themselves and how __(28)__ they felt to other individuals.
passages.zh: 在该研究中，五组参与者听取了不同的音频指令，其中一些指令鼓励参与者友善地思考自己，而另一些指令则引导他们以自我批评的方式思考。在听完音频指令后，参与者被要求回答一系列问题。这些问题包括他们是否感到焦虑不安、有多大可能对自己展现善意，以及他们感到与他人的联系有多紧密。

passages.en: The participants who were instructed to think kindly about themselves were more likely to exhibit a bodily response associated with being relaxed and feeling safe. Their heart rates also dropped, which is a healthy sign of a heart that can respond flexibly to situations. Yet, __(29)__ , those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate and sweat response afterwards, both of which __(30)__ feelings of threat and distress.
passages.zh: 被要求友善思考自己的参与者更有可能表现出与放松和感到安全相关的身体反应。他们的心率也有所下降，这是心脏能够灵活应对不同状况的健康迹象。然而相反的是，那些听了批评性音频剪辑的人随后被记录到心率更高并出现出汗反应，这两者都表明存在威胁感和痛苦感。

passages.en: Having the ability to switch off the body's natural threat response can __(31)__ a person's immune system. This, in turn, gives them a greater likelihood of recovering quickly from illness. These findings help us to further understand some of our clinical trials research findings, where we show that individuals with __(32)__ depression benefit particularly from self-awareness-based __(33)__ therapy. They essentially learn to become more sympathetic to themselves.
passages.zh: 具备关闭身体自然威胁反应的能力可以增强个人的免疫系统。这反过来使他们更有可能从疾病中快速康复。这些发现有助于我们进一步理解我们的一些临床试验研究成果，我们在其中表明，复发性抑郁症患者尤其能从基于自我意识的认知疗法中受益。他们本质上学会了对自己更加同情。

passages.en: The sense is that for people __(34)__ to depression, meeting their negative thoughts and feelings with __(35)__ is a radically different way; that these thoughts are not facts. It introduces a different way of being and knowing that is quite transformative for many people.
passages.zh: 人们认识到，对于易患抑郁症的人群而言，用同情与关怀来对待自身的负面想法和感受是一种截然不同的方式；即认识到这些想法并非事实。它引入了一种不同的存在与认知方式，这对许多人来说都具有相当大的变革意义。

rows.text: G) correlation名词
定冠词 the 后 + 介词 between 前，须填名词
explore the correlation between A and B 是固定搭配 题干 explore the __(26)__ between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state 正是研究『两个变量之间的相关性』的标准说法，correlation between A and B 在学术英语中是高频搭配。

E)compassion词义虽贴主题，但与 between A and B 搭不上 compassion 表『同情心』，不能说『探索善念与心理状态之间的同情』，逻辑不通；且 compassion 在第 35 空有更精准的归宿，留着备用。 J)insulation词义『绝缘/隔离』与研究主题完全无关 insulation 多用于物理/工程语境，放在 explore the __(26)__ between 中说『探索…之间的绝缘』明显荒谬。
B) amiably副词
动词 think 之后修饰动词，须填副词

与后文 self-critical 形成正反对照 本句结构 some of which encouraged the participants to think __(27)__ about themselves and others which persuaded them to think in a self-critical manner——前半『鼓励善待自己地想』、后半『劝其自我批判地想』，是一对反义。amiably（友好地）正与 self-critical（自我批判）相反，呼应主旨 Thinking kind thoughts about yourself。
A)adversely义为『不利地』，方向与 self-critical 同 adversely 偏负面，无法与后半 self-critical 构成对照；且第 29 空 yet 转折更需要它。 I)indignantly义为『愤慨地』，色彩负面且不合主旨 indignantly 表强烈不满，与『善待自己』完全相反，逻辑不通。
F) connected形容词
系动词 felt 后作表语，且与 how 引导的程度副词搭配
feel connected to sb 是高频固定搭配 how __(28)__ they felt to other individuals——『他们感到与他人有多紧密的联系』，feel connected to 是描述人际联结感的标准表达，与上句『对自己友善』并列考察人际维度，自然落地。
H)fascinatedfascinated 搭 by/with，不搭 to fascinated to 不构成固定搭配；语义『对他人着迷』也不符合研究问卷情境。 K)lavishlavish 不能与 felt to 搭配 lavish 表『奢华的』，无法与『对他人感到』语义对接。
A) adversely副词
句首逗号隔开的独立修饰位，副词作状语

Yet 后承接转折，需『相反地』对接前段善念组的正面反应 前段 The participants who were instructed to think kindly about themselves were more likely to exhibit a bodily response associated with being relaxed——善念组放松；本句 Yet, __(29)__, those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate——批判组反而心率升高。adversely 在此 = 『反之、不利地』，把转折讲透。
I)indignantly义为『愤慨地』，描述情绪而非研究结果走向 indignantly 只能修饰人发火的方式，不能作整句状语标示『相反走向』；不符合研究客观叙述语体。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— 考生易把 indignantly 当作『批判组』的情绪描述塞进 29 空。Yet, __(29)__, those who listened to the critical audio clips 看到『批判录音』易联想『愤慨』；防坑：本空在 Yet 后逗号夹的位置，要的是表示『反向走向』的副词（adversely），不是描述参与者情绪的副词。
N) signify动词
定语从句主语 both of which 后须填谓语动词
signify feelings of threat 表『标示/意味着…感受』 both of which __(30)__ feelings of threat and distress——心率与出汗反应『标示着威胁与痛苦的感受』，signify 正是『作为…的标志/表征』的常用动词，与生理指标作为情绪指标的科学表述完全契合。
O)surpass义为『超过』，与情绪感受无法搭配 surpass feelings of threat 表『超越威胁感』，宾语与动词意义不匹配，逻辑荒谬。
C) boost动词
情态动词 can 后须接动词原形

boost the immune system 是固定搭配 can __(31)__ a person's immune system. This, in turn, gives them a greater likelihood of recovering quickly from illness——『增强免疫系统，从而更易病愈』，boost the immune system 是健康/医学语境中的固定表达，逻辑链清晰。
N)signify义为『表示/意味着』，与『对免疫系统起作用』语义错位 signify the immune system 表『标示免疫系统』，不通；且 N 在第 30 空有更精确的归宿。 O)surpass义为『超过』，宾语与免疫系统逻辑不符 surpass one's immune system 表『超越其免疫系统』，无意义。
M) recurrent形容词
with 后修饰 depression 的前置定语

recurrent depression 是临床精确术语 individuals with __(32)__ depression benefit particularly from self-awareness-based cognitive therapy 说的是抑郁症患者中的某一亚群——『反复发作型抑郁』（recurrent depression）正是医学/心理学专业术语，且与下段 meeting their negative thoughts and feelings 中『反复出现的负性念头』自洽。

F)connected义为『相连的』，与 depression 搭不上 没有 connected depression 这种表述。 H)fascinated形容人感受，不能修饰疾病 fascinated depression 不通。 K)lavish色彩与疾病不符 lavish 表『奢华的』，不修饰病症。 L)proneprone 不前置修饰名词 prone 多作表语 be prone to；且需留给第 34 空 prone to depression。
D) cognitive形容词
self-awareness-based 与 therapy 之间，须填形容词作前置定语
cognitive therapy 是心理学术语固定搭配 self-awareness-based __(33)__ therapy——『基于自我觉察的认知疗法』是临床心理学权威术语 cognitive therapy / CBT 的直接对应，与下句 learn to become more sympathetic to themselves 的认知重构思路完全吻合。

F)connected义为『相连的』，与 therapy 搭不上 没有 connected therapy 这种说法；且 connected 留待第 28 空 feel connected 用。 H)fascinated形容人，不能修饰 therapy fascinated 一般表『（人）着迷的』，主语应是 someone is fascinated；放在 therapy 前不成立。 K)lavish义为『奢华的/过度的』，色彩不符 lavish therapy 不是临床术语，也与『自我觉察』的内省语境不搭。 L)proneprone 后常接 to，作表语，不作前置定语 标准结构是 be prone to N；几乎不放在名词前作 prone therapy；且留待第 34 空 prone to depression。 M)recurrent义为『反复发作的』，与 therapy 逻辑不符 recurrent 修饰的是疾病/症状（recurrent depression），不修饰疗法本身；且留待第 32 空。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— 考生易被 self-awareness-based 这串复合形容词带跑而选 connected。self-awareness-based __(33)__ therapy 中，看到『自我觉察』易联想『联结』而选 connected；防坑：心理学『___ therapy』 类术语优先匹配 cognitive，且 connected 留作 28 空的 feel connected to 才合理。
L) prone形容词
for people 后修饰 people 的后置定语，且后接 to depression
be prone to depression 是固定搭配 for people __(34)__ to depression——『易患抑郁的人群』，prone to + N 表『易于/倾向于（不好的事）』，与抑郁这种负面色彩完美匹配。

F)connectedconnected 搭 with/to 都不表示『易患』 connected to depression 只表示『与抑郁相关』，不表『易患』，语义弱且偏题。 H)fascinatedfascinated to depression 不成立 fascinated 通常搭 by/with，不搭 to；且『对抑郁着迷』逻辑荒谬。 K)lavishlavish 不搭 to，色彩也反 lavish 没有 lavish to 的固定结构。
E) compassion名词
介词 with 后须接名词作宾语

与主旨『善待自己』扣合，meet ... with compassion 是地道搭配 meeting their negative thoughts and feelings with __(35)__——『以慈悲心面对自己的负面念头与感受』，与全文主线 Thinking kind thoughts about yourself 完全一致；且呼应 They essentially learn to become more sympathetic to themselves。
J)insulation义为『绝缘』，与情感主题完全脱节 with insulation 表『用绝缘材料』，物理工程语境，放进心理学语境荒谬。

longreading.title: 2022年6月·第2套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) In the long view, the human relationship with forests has been one of brutal destruction, but even it carries elements of slow hope. In the Middle Ages, there was no shortage of timber in most parts of the world, and few saw cutting down forests as a problem. Yet in 1548 the people of Venice estimated that an important timber supply would last only 30 years at their current rate of usage—but different forest management would make it possible to meet the demand for many centuries to come. The idea of preserving resources came out of a concern for the future: a fear of using up resources faster than they could be replenished(补充).
passages.zh: 从长远来看，人类与森林的关系一直是残酷的破坏，但其中也包含着缓慢希望的因素。在中世纪，世界大部分地区并不缺少木材，很少有人认为砍伐森林是个问题。然而，1548年，威尼斯民众估计，按照当时的使用速度，一项重要的木材供应只能维持30年；但如果采取不同的森林管理方式，就有可能满足未来许多个世纪的需求。保护资源的理念源于对未来的忧虑：人们担心资源的消耗速度会快于其补充速度。

passages.en: B) Economic interests were at the core of this understanding of trees and forests. It would take more than three centuries before scientists began to understand that timber production is not the only, and possibly not the most important, function of forests. The late 19th and early 20th century saw an increasing recognition that forests serve as habitats for countless animal and plant species that all rely on each other. They take over protective functions against soil erosion and landslides(塌方); they make a significant contribution to the water balance as they prevent surface runoff; they filter dirt particles, greenhouse gases and radioactive substances from the air; they produce oxygen; they provide spaces for recreation and they preserve historic and prehistoric remains. As a result, forests around the world have been set aside as parks or wilderness areas.
passages.zh: 经济利益是这种树木和森林观念的核心。科学家花了三个多世纪才开始认识到，木材生产并不是森林唯一的功能，而且可能也不是最重要的功能。19世纪末和20世纪初，人们日益认识到，森林是无数动植物物种的栖息地，而这些物种彼此依赖。森林具有防止水土流失和塌方的保护功能；它们能够防止地表径流，对水量平衡作出重要贡献；它们可以过滤空气中的尘粒、温室气体和放射性物质；它们能够产生氧气；它们为休闲活动提供空间，并保存历史和史前遗迹。因此，世界各地的森林被划为公园或荒野地区。

passages.en: C) Recent years have seen a big change in our view of forests. Peter Wohlleben's book The Hidden Life of Trees (2015), an international bestseller, suggests that trees can warn each other of danger through a "wood wide web" of roots and fungi(真菌). They support each other through sharing of nutrients and information, and they even keep ancient stumps alive by feeding them solutions of sugars. Such insights have made us aware of deep ecological relationships between humans and the more-than-human world.
passages.zh: 近年来，我们对森林的看法发生了巨大变化。彼得·沃勒本的著作《树的秘密生命》（2015年）是一本国际畅销书，书中提出，树木可以通过由根系和真菌构成的“木联网”彼此预警。它们通过分享养分和信息相互支持，甚至会通过向古老的树桩输送糖溶液来维持它们的生命。这些认识使我们意识到人类与超越人类的世界之间存在着深层的生态联系。

passages.en: D) Awareness of ecologies is a recent phenomenon. It was not until the 1940s that the concept of the "environment" embracing all living and nonliving things developed. In the 1970s, the term "environment" gained currency, becoming widely adopted in the English and Romance languages, and as "Umwelt" ("surrounding world") in German. The emergence of the idea led to the rise of environmental agencies, regulations and environmental studies, and to environmental science as new, integrated academic disciplines. It was in 1956 that the very first bachelor of science in environmental studies was awarded, at the State University of New York College of Forestry at Syracuse. Since the 1970s—with the rise of "environmentalism"—environmental studies programmes have sprung up at hundreds of universities. There is (slow) hope in the fact that scholars from many different disciplines have adopted the term "environment" over the past decades. They are exploring intricate connections within and between complex ecologies, as well as the impact that human environment-making (through techno-industrial, economic and other manipulative developments) has had on the biosphere.
passages.zh: 对生态系统的认识是最近才出现的现象。直到20世纪40年代，“环境”这一涵盖所有有生命和无生命事物的概念才形成。20世纪70年代，“环境”一词开始流行，并被英语和罗曼语族语言广泛采用；在德语中则称为“Umwelt”（意为“周围的世界”）。这一理念的出现推动了环境机构、环境法规和环境研究的发展，也促成了环境科学这一新的综合性学科。1956年，第一位环境研究理学学士在纽约州立大学锡拉丘兹林学院获得学位。自20世纪70年代“环保主义”兴起以来，数百所大学纷纷设立环境研究项目。过去几十年来，来自许多不同学科的学者都采用了“环境”这一术语，这一事实体现了（缓慢的）希望。他们正在探索复杂生态系统内部以及不同复杂生态系统之间错综复杂的联系，同时研究人类通过技术工业、经济及其他操控性发展塑造环境，对生物圈所产生的影响。

passages.en: E) The rise of the idea of the environment and a scholarly understanding of ecological processes has influenced new technologies and also politics. We have come to ask questions about vulnerability and risk, world ecologies, and the relationship between nature and power. The search for an adequate response to climate change occupies centre stage in international diplomacy.
passages.zh: 环境理念的兴起以及对生态过程的学术认识，影响了新技术，也影响了政治。我们开始提出有关脆弱性与风险、全球生态系统以及自然与权力之间关系的问题。寻求应对气候变化的恰当方案，已成为国际外交的核心议题。

passages.en: F) Social and environmental activists, scientists and indigenous groups have called the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Climate Change Conference in December 2015 insufficient, weak, or compromised. To some extent, they are right: climate change has already destroyed tens of thousands of livelihoods, and the situation will worsen in the near future for millions of mostly poorer people, who will join the ranks of those who have already been displaced by climate change and extreme weather events. But the Paris Conference nevertheless marked a historic step toward the recognition of the need for action on climate change, the cutting of carbon emissions, and world cooperation. There were 195 nations that came to the table in Paris and agreed to limits on emissions. Historically, nothing comparable had happened prior to this. Before the 20th century, a handful of scientists had been interested in the theoretical relationship between greenhouse gases and climate change, but only the empirical evidence accumulated since the late 20th century established a clear connection between the burning of fossil fuels and a vastly accelerated rise in global temperatures.
passages.zh: 社会和环境活动人士、科学家以及原住民团体认为，2015年12月联合国气候变化大会达成的《巴黎协定》不充分、软弱或存在妥协。在某种程度上，他们是对的：气候变化已经摧毁了数以万计人的生计；在不久的将来，数百万主要来自较贫困群体的人将面临更加恶化的处境，并加入那些已经因气候变化和极端天气事件而流离失所者的行列。然而，巴黎大会仍然标志着人们认识到必须采取气候行动、削减碳排放并开展全球合作，向前迈出了历史性的一步。共有195个国家来到巴黎谈判桌前，并同意限制排放。从历史上看，此前从未发生过与之相 comparable 的事情。20世纪以前，只有少数科学家关注温室气体与气候变化之间的理论关系；但直到20世纪末以来不断积累的实证证据，才确立了化石燃料燃烧与全球气温大幅加速上升之间的明确联系。

passages.en: G) The current crisis is not the first that humans have encountered, and a look at the struggles with pollution in recent history reveals transformations that once seemed unimaginable. The "London fog" that came to define the capital through British novels and thrillers is in reality smog or smoke, a legacy of industrialisation. After a century of ignorance, London was hit by the Great Smog of December 1952—the worst air-pollution event in the history of the United Kingdom which caused the deaths of approximately 12,000 people. Shortly thereafter, public initiatives and political campaigns led to strict regulations and new laws, including the Clean Air Act (1956). Today, London has effectively reduced traffic emissions through the introduction of a Congestion Charge Zone in 2003, and an Ultra Low Emission Zone in 2019.
passages.zh: 当前的危机并不是人类遭遇的第一次危机，而回顾近代历史上与污染的斗争，可以发现一些曾经令人难以想象的转变。通过英国小说和惊悚作品而成为这座首都标志的“伦敦雾”，实际上是工业化遗留下来的烟雾污染。经过一个世纪的漠视，伦敦在1952年12月遭遇了大烟雾事件，这是英国历史上最严重的空气污染事件，造成约1.2万人死亡。不久之后，公众倡议和政治运动推动了严格的监管和新法律的出台，其中包括《清洁空气法》（1956年）。如今，伦敦通过2003年设立拥堵收费区以及2019年设立超低排放区，有效减少了交通排放。

passages.en: H) Scientific evidence that we are living in an era of climate change, resource exhaustion and potential ecological disaster is overwhelming. How do we motivate a public exhausted by never-ending scenarios of doom and disaster, when the challenges seem so huge and so impossible to solve? Statistics about extinction and the gloom of decline will not in themselves get us out of our often self-created ecological traps: instead, they are more likely to result in paralysis and inaction.
passages.zh: 科学证据表明，我们正生活在一个气候变化、资源枯竭和潜在生态灾难的时代，这些证据是压倒性的。当挑战看起来如此巨大、如此不可能解决时，面对没完没了的厄运和灾难预言已经疲惫不堪的公众，我们该如何激发他们的行动动力？有关物种灭绝和衰退阴影的统计数据本身并不能使我们摆脱那些往往由自己造成的生态陷阱；相反，它们更可能导致瘫痪和无所作为。

passages.en: I) We need stories and histories of change and transformation: ecological stories that make us confront the fact that human power is potentially destructive, and that the survival of our species on this planet depends on the preservation of soil and water, and the habitats and ecological systems.
passages.zh: 我们需要关于变化和转型的故事与历史：需要生态故事，促使我们正视这样一个事实，即人类的力量具有潜在的破坏性，而我们这个物种能否在地球上生存下去，取决于土壤和水，以及栖息地和生态系统的保护。

passages.en: J) It is time that we showed successes and accelerations in ecological awareness, action and restoration: stories that include past successes and future visions about the rise of urban gardening and of renaturalised riverscapes, of successful protests against polluted air and water, of the rise of regional markets and slow food, and the planting of trees around the globe, of initiatives and enterprises that work towards ecological restoration. The reality of ecological curses seems far greater than the power of the hopes left at the bottom of Pandora's box. But if we believe that nothing can be changed, then we are giving up our opportunity to act.
passages.zh: 现在是我们展示生态意识、生态行动和生态修复方面的成就与加速发展的时刻了：这些故事应包括过去的成功和对未来的设想，如城市园艺和河流自然化景观的兴起，如反对空气和水污染的抗议取得成功，如区域市场和慢食的兴起，如在全球各地植树，以及那些致力于生态修复的倡议和企业。生态灾难的现实似乎远远超过了潘多拉魔盒底部所剩希望的力量。但如果我们相信什么都无法改变，那么我们就是在放弃行动的机会。

passages.en: K) Today's saving powers will not come from a deus ex machina(解围之神). In an ever-more complex and synthetic world, our saving powers won't come from a single source, and certainly not from a too-big-to-fail approach or from those who have been drawn into the whirlpool of our age of speed. Hope can work as a wakeup call. It acknowledges setbacks. The concept of slow hope suggests that we can't expect things to change overnight. If the ever-faster exhaustion of natural resources (in ecological terms) and the "shrinking of the present" (in social terms) are urgent problems of humans, then cutting down on exhaustive practices and working towards a "stretching of the present" will be ways to move forward.
passages.zh: 今天拯救我们的力量不会来自解围之神。在一个日益复杂且合成化的世界里，拯救我们的力量不会来自单一来源，当然也不会来自“大到不能倒”的做法，或来自那些被卷入我们这个高速时代漩涡的人。希望可以发挥唤醒我们的作用。它承认挫折的存在。“缓慢的希望”这一概念表明，我们不能指望事情在一夜之间发生改变。如果自然资源以越来越快的速度耗竭（就生态学而言），以及“现在的收缩”（就社会而言）是人类面临的紧迫问题，那么减少耗竭性行为，并努力实现“现在的延展”，将是我们前进的途径。

passages.en: Since American idol star Taryn Southern started composing music with AI in 2017, musicians all over the world have begun wondering about the implications of AI and modern technology where music production is concerned. Using AI in the creation of music is perceived by some as a helpful tool and by others as almost "the beginning of the end".
passages.zh: 自2017年美国偶像明星Taryn Southern开始使用人工智能创作音乐以来，世界各地的音乐家都开始思考人工智能和现代技术对音乐制作的影响。有人认为，利用人工智能创作音乐是一种有用的工具；而另一些人则认为，这几乎是“末日的开始”。

passages.en: In Taryn's case, AI software enabled her to communicate melodies and chords that she didn't know how to put together herself. The end product was therefore a collaborative effort, rather than a piece entirely produced by technology. Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block(文思枯竭).
passages.zh: 就Taryn而言，人工智能软件使她能够表达出旋律和和弦，而她自己并不知道如何将它们组合起来。因此，最终作品是合作完成的成果，而不是完全由技术制作的作品。Taryn的故事明显带有积极色彩，突出了在音乐制作中使用人工智能的优势。它可以成为灵感的来源，也可以在音乐家陷入文思枯竭时，作为一个理想的起点。

passages.en: Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene. At the moment, because such technology is still so young, the music it's producing is not necessarily what we want to hear. In short, it's not of great quality. Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician.
passages.zh: 与将人工智能视为工具的看法相反，一些音乐家认为它会对音乐界造成极大的损害。目前，由于这项技术还很年轻，它创作出的音乐未必是我们想听的。简而言之，其质量并不高。那些创作过自己的音乐的人，甚至是真正喜爱艺术性音乐的乐迷，也会认为计算机永远无法模仿真正音乐家的作品以及其中的人性触感。

passages.en: Music has been an integral part of the story of humans for ages; in fact, the first known piece of music is believed to be around 3,400 years old. Songs have long been used as a means of communicating messages and folk stories, covering everything from societal ethics to world history. Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology. The thought of a computer generating a "random" piece of music that hasn't been painstakingly created by an artist is almost seen as sacrilegious(亵渎神圣的).
passages.zh: 数千年来，音乐一直是人类发展历程中不可或缺的一部分；事实上，已知最早的音乐作品据认为已有约3400年的历史。长期以来，歌曲一直被用来传达信息和民间故事，内容涵盖社会伦理到世界历史的方方面面。由于许多人认为音乐是一种与生俱来的人类表达方式，因此常常觉得它过于珍贵，不应交给技术。人们几乎认为，让计算机生成一段未经艺术家精心创作的“随机”音乐，是一种亵渎神圣的行为。

passages.en: Regardless of which side of the argument you fall on, it seems likely that the use of AI in music production will only become more frequent. Our modern world is preoccupied with technological advancements. Instead of shying away from the idea of this bleak future, the best approach to take is one of optimism and curiosity. While there are always bound to be stubborn old-school musicians who refuse to use tech, music producers should consider AI as something to be embraced. AI music software is still very much in its infancy, but with more investors interested in the development and outcomes of such technology, and considering the rapid growth rate of other tech advances in recent years, it's only a matter of time before AI-produced music is seen as the new norm.
passages.zh: 无论你支持哪一方的观点，人工智能在音乐制作中的使用似乎都只会越来越频繁。我们这个现代世界十分关注技术进步。与其回避这个黯淡未来的想法，不如采取乐观且充满好奇心的态度。尽管总会有一些顽固的老派音乐家拒绝使用科技，但音乐制作人应当考虑接受人工智能。人工智能音乐软件仍处于非常初级的阶段，但随着越来越多的投资者对这项技术的发展及其成果感兴趣，再考虑到近年来其他技术进步的快速发展速度，人工智能创作的音乐被视为新常态只是时间问题。

questions.判型: 题干How do some musicians perceive using AI in creating music?问"一部分音乐人如何看待"，是对原文中明示观点句的客观转述，属于细节题而非推断题。
questions.拆句: How do some musicians perceive using AI in creating music? 主干是 some musicians perceive X，X 是动名词短语 using AI in creating music。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene. 与把 AI 视作工具的看法相反，一些音乐人认为它对音乐界极为有害。

locate.en: Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene.
locate.zh: 与把 AI 视作工具的看法相反，一些音乐人认为它对音乐界极为有害。

option_analysis.note: 原文首段提到 American idol star Taryn Southern 是引子人名，与音乐人对 AI 的看法无关；produce more music idols 拿这一无关词造句，属无中生有。
预判得到"对音乐创作有害"，It would be detrimental to music production 是其逐词同义改写，最直接对应，故选 B。

pairs.orig: hugely detrimental to the music scene

option_analysis.note: 反对派担心的是 AI not necessarily what we want to hear"产出质量"和never emulate the work"复刻原创"，从未说过 AI 会妨碍"听众理解"真正的音乐；hinder the understanding of authentic music 把动作对象从"产出"偷换为"理解"。
the beginning of a new era"新时代的开端"是正向积极评价，而原文反对派恰恰说的是 the beginning of the end"终结的开端"——选项把 end 偷换成 new era，方向完全相反。

questions.stem: What does Taryn Southern's story illustrate?
questions.stem_zh: Taryn Southern的故事说明了什么?

options.text: AI technology is conducive to music composition.
options.zh: 人工智能技术有利于音乐创作。

options.text: Musicians will be unable to create music without high tech.
options.zh: 音乐人如果没有高科技将无法创作音乐。

options.text: Musicians are often at their wits' end in their creative effort.
options.zh: 音乐人在创作过程中常常束手无策。

options.text: AI technology is indispensable to creating melodies and chords.
options.zh: 人工智能技术对于创作旋律和和弦是必不可少的。

questions.判型: 题干结构是"具体人物故事 + illustrate"，问例子的服务对象，是典型的例证目的题。
questions.拆句: What does Taryn Southern's story illustrate? 主干 What does X illustrate，X 是 Taryn Southern's story。结构简单，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block. Taryn 的故事带有明显的积极意味，凸显出在音乐创作中使用 AI 的种种好处。它可以作为灵感的源泉，并且在音乐人遭遇文思枯竭时，是一个理想的起点。

locate.en: Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block.
locate.zh: Taryn 的故事带有明显的积极意味，凸显出在音乐创作中使用 AI 的种种好处。它可以作为灵感的源泉，并且在音乐人遭遇文思枯竭时，是一个理想的起点。

option_analysis.note: 预判得到"AI 有助于音乐创作"，AI technology is conducive to music composition 精确对应，故选 A。

pairs.orig: highlights the advantages of using AI in music production

option_analysis.note: 原文只说 AI 是"协作工具""灵感来源"，从未说"没有高科技就无法创作"；unable to create music without high tech 是把"有帮助"夸大成"不可或缺"。
原文只说"如果"音乐人遇到 writer's block，AI 是一个 jumping-off point；选项 often at their wits' end"经常技穷"把假设条件偷换为普遍现象，且偏离例证目的。
原文称 AI 是 source of inspiration 与 jumping-off point——是"加分项"，而 indispensable to creating melodies and chords"不可或缺"把作用拔高到"必需"，与原文协作性定位不符。

questions.stem: Why are some musicians opposed to the use of AI in creating music?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么一些音乐人反对在音乐创作中使用人工智能?

options.text: Music produced with AI technology lacks humanness.
options.zh: 用人工智能技术制作的音乐缺乏人性。

options.text: Music created with AI technology is easily emulated.
options.zh: 用人工智能技术创作的音乐很容易被模仿。

options.text: It will depreciate humans' role in music composition.
options.zh: 这将贬低人类在音乐创作中的作用。

options.text: It will deplete young musicians, creative inspiration.
options.zh: 这将耗尽年轻音乐人的创作灵感。

questions.判型: 题干以 Why 提问反对的原因，答案应是原文里反对派给出的明确理由句的同义改写。
questions.拆句: Why are some musicians opposed to the use of AI in creating music? be opposed to 是固定搭配=反对。主干清晰。
questions.定位: P3 Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician. 那些自己创作过音乐的人，甚至是真正的艺术音乐爱好者也会争辩说，电脑永远无法复刻一位真正音乐人的作品（以及那种人性温度）。

locate.en: Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician.
locate.zh: 那些自己创作过音乐的人，甚至是真正的艺术音乐爱好者也会争辩说，电脑永远无法复刻一位真正音乐人的作品（以及那种人性温度）。

option_analysis.note: 预判"缺人性"与 Music produced with AI technology lacks humanness 完全等价，故选 A。

pairs.orig: a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician

option_analysis.note: 原文说"电脑无法 emulate 真正音乐人"——是 AI 模仿不来人；选项 easily emulated"AI 音乐容易被模仿"把模仿的主客关系颠倒，且 easily 与原文 never 直接相反。
depreciate humans' role"贬低人类在音乐创作中的角色"虽然在情感上和反对派接近，但原文给出的反对理由是"复刻不出人性"而非"会贬低人类角色"——本题问的是 Why 反对，必须是原文实际给出的理由。
原文从未提到 AI 会"耗尽年轻音乐人的创作灵感"，deplete young musicians, creative inspiration 是凭空造话。注意 P2 提到 AI 是"灵感来源"——正好相反。

questions.stem: Why do many people think music is too precious to impart to AI technology?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么许多人认为音乐太宝贵而不能传授给人工智能技术?

options.text: It cannot be created without pains.
options.zh: 音乐不能不经过辛苦就创作出来。

options.text: It cannot be produced at random.
options.zh: 音乐不能随意产生。

options.text: It is part of human life.
options.zh: 音乐是人类生活的一部分。

options.text: It is human specific.
options.zh: 音乐是人类特有的。

questions.判型: 题干问"为何认为音乐太珍贵不能交给AI"，是对原文给出理由的客观转述。
questions.拆句: Why do many people think music is too precious to impart to AI technology? 嵌套 think 宾语从句；too…to… 表示"太…以致不能"；impart to=交付给。理解关键是 too…to… 的否定意味。
questions.定位: P4 Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology. 因为许多人把音乐视为人类固有的一种表达方式，所以它常被认为太珍贵了，不应交付给技术。

locate.en: Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology.
locate.zh: 因为许多人把音乐视为人类固有的一种表达方式，所以它常被认为太珍贵了，不应交付给技术。

option_analysis.note: 原文用 painstakingly"煞费苦心"形容真正音乐人的创作，强调过程不易；cannot be created without pains"没有痛苦就无法创作"虽与文本有触点，但本题问的是"为何太珍贵"，答案应是"音乐属于人类"，而不是"创作过程辛苦"。
原文说"电脑生成 random 的音乐被视为亵渎"，并非"音乐不能随机产生"；cannot be produced at random 把原文的 random（贬义形容词修饰AI产品）偷换为"产生方式"的逻辑命题，且并非太珍贵的理由。

part of human life"是人类生活的一部分"虽然符合原文"陪伴人类多年"的事实（integral part of the story of humans for ages），但本题问的是"为何太珍贵"，关键论点是"人类专属"而非"陪伴时间长"。Part of human life 比 human specific 弱：很多东西都是"人类生活的一部分"（如食物、衣物），未必只属人类——这恰恰落不到"专属"的关键力度。
预判"音乐是人类专属"与 It is human specific 完全等价，故选 D。

questions.stem: What does the author think of the future of AI music?
questions.stem_zh: 作者如何看待人工智能音乐的未来?

options.text: It will continue to arouse the interest of music investors.
options.zh: 它将继续引起音乐投资者的兴趣。

options.text: It has the prospect of becoming the norm in the future.
options.zh: 它有望在未来成为常态。

options.text: It will be gradually accepted by old-school musicians.
options.zh: 它将逐渐被传统派音乐人接受。

options.text: It may eventually lose its freshness and appeal.
options.zh: 它最终可能会失去新鲜感和吸引力。

questions.判型: 题干问作者怎么看，是对作者主观立场的探测，属态度/观点题。
questions.拆句: What does the author think of the future of AI music? think of=对…怎么看；of 引出态度对象。主干平铺。

option_analysis.note: continue to arouse the interest of music investors 投资者的兴趣，在原文 with more investors interested in the development 中只是作者用来支持"AI 音乐必成常态"的论据，本身不是作者对"未来"的核心判断；本题问 What does the author think of the future，答案要选最终判断而不是中间论据。
预判"AI 音乐终将成为常态"与 It has the prospect of becoming the norm in the future 同义，故选 B。

pairs.orig: it's only a matter of time before AI-produced music is seen as the new norm
pairs.opt: has the prospect of becoming the norm in the future

option_analysis.note: 原文 there are always bound to be stubborn old-school musicians who refuse to use tech 明确指出守旧派始终会拒绝技术；gradually accepted by old-school musicians 反过来说他们会"逐渐接受"，与原文 refuse 直接相反。
may eventually lose its freshness and appeal"最终失去新鲜感和吸引力"——原文从未提到 AI 音乐会失去吸引力，反而判断它会成为新常态。属凭空构造。

reading2.title: 2022年6月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: A few weeks ago, a well-meaning professor tried to explain the physiological process behind viruses and the human body in a tweet and was immediately criticized for a mistake in his information. He then issued an apology and deleted his erroneous tweet.
passages.zh: 几周前，一位善意的教授试图在一条推文中解释病毒与人体背后的生理过程，却因信息中的一处错误立即受到批评。随后，他发表道歉声明，并删除了那条错误的推文。

passages.en: Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions.
passages.zh: 将科学传播到学术圈之外，对于增进公众对健康和环境问题的理解，以及帮助个人作出充分知情的决定，都是必要的。

passages.en: However, scientists who engage in science communication must acknowledge that even in their area, their expertise is deep but narrow. They need to recognize the constraints in their own knowledge. That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline. Fact-checking with a scientist who works in the specialty will prevent the unintentional spread of misinformation, and the process of doing so may yield tiny pieces of interesting new information that can be incorporated.
passages.zh: 然而，参与科学传播的科学家必须承认，即使在自己的领域内，他们的专业知识也是深而窄的。他们需要认识到自身知识的局限。这并不是说他们只能围绕自己的研究进行写作或演讲，而是说，如果主题超出自己的学科范围，就应当向相关专家咨询。请该专业领域的科学家进行事实核查，可以防止无意中传播错误信息，而这一过程也可能产生一些有趣的新信息片段，并将其纳入传播内容。

passages.en: Some have argued that the public is not educated enough to understand scientific information, especially for any complex phenomena, but this is absurd. Science instruction can be found at all levels of public education with most secondary schools offering classes on biology, physics, and chemistry. If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles.
passages.zh: 有人认为，公众没有受过足够的教育，无法理解科学信息，尤其是那些复杂的科学现象，但这种说法十分荒谬。公共教育的各个阶段都设有科学教学，大多数中学还开设生物学、物理学和化学课程。恰恰相反，社交媒体表明，公众渴望获得建立在坚实科学基础上的知识。大多数科学文章发表后引发的公众讨论甚至表明，网络读者能够理解最令人困惑的科学原理。

passages.en: It is equally imperative to emphasize that being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience. A number of scientists recently have been offering public-aimed explanations of scientific phenomena. Even though they have appropriate credentials, they often do very little in the way of explaining. One biologist shared an intricate analogy involving a library, books, paper, a recipe, ingredients, and a cake to explain the process behind vaccines. Any explanation that requires a written key to keep track of what each item represents is not a clear example for public consumption.
passages.zh: 同样必须强调的是，成为某一主题的专家，并不会自动使学者具备向非科学受众进行讲解的资格。最近，不少科学家一直在面向公众解释科学现象。尽管他们拥有相应的资历，但在解释方面往往做得很少。一位生物学家曾用一个涉及图书馆、书籍、纸张、食谱、配料和蛋糕的复杂类比，来解释疫苗背后的原理。任何需要借助一份书面说明来记住每件物品分别代表什么的解释，都不是一个适合公众理解的清晰范例。

passages.en: Science communication is a science in and of itself. It requires rigorous training and instruction. A scientist should take communication courses that can teach a person how to identify and eliminate jargon and how to develop effective analogies to explain complex concepts. One cannot assume communication expertise—imagine if someone just decided that they were a physicist and started trying to contribute to the field without the necessary background. Doing a poor job communicating science to the public will only create confusion and widen the gap between science and society, a gap that scientists are trying to close.
passages.zh: 科学传播本身就是一门科学。它需要严格的培训和指导。科学家应当参加传播课程，学习如何识别并消除术语，以及如何构建有效的类比来解释复杂概念。不能想当然地认为自己具备传播方面的专业能力——试想，如果有人只是决定自己是一名物理学家，然后在没有必要背景知识的情况下开始试图为这一领域作出贡献，会是怎样的情形。向公众进行糟糕的科学传播只会造成混乱，扩大科学与社会之间的鸿沟，而科学家正努力弥合这一鸿沟。

questions.stem: What does the author say about communicating science to the general public?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对向公众传播科学有何看法?

options.text: It will help them to keep abreast of the latest scientific developments.
options.zh: 这将帮助他们跟上最新的科学发展。

options.text: It is a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues.
options.zh: 这是提高他们对科学问题理解的必要手段。

options.text: It will get them more involved in academic debates on environmental problems.
options.zh: 这将使他们更多地参与关于环境问题的学术辩论。

options.text: It is an effective way to augment scientists' influence beyond the academic circle.
options.zh: 这是增强科学家在学术圈之外影响力的有效方式。

questions.判型: What does the author say about communicating science to the general public? 问的是「作者对某话题说了什么」，要求回到原文找出作者关于这件事的明确表态，属于细节理解。
questions.拆句: Q51 是简单的 What 引导特殊疑问句，主干是 the author say about 后接动名词短语 communicating science to the general public，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions. 把科学传播到学术圈外，是增进公众对健康与环境议题理解、帮助个人做出明智决策的必要途径。

locate.en: Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions.
locate.zh: 把科学传播到学术圈外，是增进公众对健康与环境议题理解、帮助个人做出明智决策的必要途径。

option_analysis.note: keep abreast of the latest scientific developments 把「最新科学进展」塞进选项，而 P2 只说提升理解、辅助决策，从未提及 latest developments。
a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues 同时命中预判的「必要性」与「提升理解」两条语义槽，无多余成分，是定位句的标准同义改写。

pairs.orig: necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues
pairs.opt: a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues

option_analysis.note: get them more involved in academic debates on environmental problems 把原文「帮助个人做明智决策」偷换为「让公众参与学术辩论」，方向完全相反——原文恰恰是要把科学带到学术圈外，而非把公众拉进学术辩论。
augment scientists' influence beyond the academic circle 把「augment 的对象」从原文的 public understanding 偷换为 scientists' influence——augment 这个词留下了，受益人却换了，是典型「同词不同对象」陷阱。

questions.stem: What does the author advise scientists to do to deal with topics outside of their specialty?
questions.stem_zh: 作者建议科学家如何处理其专业领域之外的话题?

options.text: Write or present on them from new angles.
options.zh: 从新的角度撰写或阐述这些话题。

options.text: Utilize information from diverse sources.
options.zh: 利用来自不同来源的信息。

options.text: Turn to a specialist for professional help.
options.zh: 向专业人士寻求专业帮助。

options.text: Fact-check with colleagues in their field.
options.zh: 与其领域的同事进行事实核查。

questions.判型: What does the author advise scientists to do to deal with topics outside of their specialty? 直接问「作者建议做什么」，是对原文具体建议句的事实复述。
questions.拆句: Q52 主干 What does the author advise scientists to do，后接不定式短语 to deal with topics outside of their specialty 表目的，整体直白。
questions.定位: P3 That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline. 这并不是说他们只能写或讲自己的研究，而是说，如果话题超出本人学科范围，他们应当请教该领域专家。

locate.en: That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline.
locate.zh: 这并不是说他们只能写或讲自己的研究，而是说，如果话题超出本人学科范围，他们应当请教该领域专家。

option_analysis.note: Write or present on them from new angles 凭空加入 new angles 这一限定，原文 they only write or present on their own research 是作者要排除的误读，且无任何「新角度」之意。
Utilize information from diverse sources 把作者明确指出的「咨询专家 + 事实核查」泛化为「使用多元来源信息」，方向被悄悄稀释——作者强调的是「找对人」，不是「找够多源头」。
Turn to a specialist for professional help 把预判的「请教 + 该领域专家」两要素逐一对上，且 specialist 与 specialty 同根，符合作者「领域内行家」的限定。

pairs.orig: consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline
pairs.opt: Turn to a specialist for professional help

option_analysis.note: Fact-check with colleagues in their field 保留 Fact-check 这一动词（直接借自原文 Fact-checking with a scientist who works in the specialty），但把对象偷换为 colleagues in their field——原文恰恰强调因为话题在 their field 之外，才要找该话题所在领域（specialty）的专家。

questions.stem: What does the author say we can learn from social media?
questions.stem_zh: 作者说我们能从社交媒体中学到什么?

options.text: A solid academic foundation is essential to understanding baffling scientific principles.
options.zh: 扎实的学术基础对于理解令人困惑的科学原理至关重要。

options.text: Modern technology has facilitated communication between scientists and the public.
options.zh: 现代技术促进了科学家与公众之间的交流。

options.text: Scientific articles have gained increasing popularity among the general public.
options.zh: 科学文章在公众中越来越受欢迎。

options.text: The public's understanding of science is much better than some have claimed.

questions.判型: What does the author say we can learn from social media? 问的是「从某事例中能得出什么结论」，本质仍是回到原文找作者就 social media 给出的论断句，属于细节而非推断。
questions.拆句: Q53 主干 What… we can learn from social media，宾语从句简单，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles. 如果说有什么的话，社交媒体反而表明，公众渴望以扎实科学基础为支撑的知识。甚至大多数科学文章后面的公众讨论都显示，在线读者能够理解最难懂的科学原理。

locate.en: If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles.
locate.zh: 如果说有什么的话，社交媒体反而表明，公众渴望以扎实科学基础为支撑的知识。甚至大多数科学文章后面的公众讨论都显示，在线读者能够理解最难懂的科学原理。

option_analysis.note: A solid academic foundation is essential to understanding baffling scientific principles 把原文「公众渴望基于科学的知识」误读为「必须具备学术根基才能理解科学」——原文是「公众主动 craves 知识」，不是「没有 foundation 就不行」。
Modern technology has facilitated communication between scientists and the public 把 social media 上位概括为 modern technology，又把「公众理解力」偷换为「双向沟通」，原文从未谈及 facilitated communication。

It is imperative to have appropriate titles to explain scientific issues 把原文 appropriate credentials 偷换为 appropriate titles，且作者强调的恰恰是「光有 credentials 不够」，本选项反而说「必须有合适头衔」，方向与作者完全相反。

option_analysis.note: Explain complex concepts scientifically 把建议对象偷换为「科学地解释复杂概念」——原文要做的恰好相反，是用 effective analogies 把复杂概念变得通俗，而不是「更科学地」讲。
Make appropriate use of scientific terms 与作者建议背道而驰——原文明确说 identify and eliminate jargon，选项却让科学家「合理使用术语」，方向反置。
Take courses in public speaking 把原文 communication courses 偷换为 public speaking——「沟通课」覆盖书面/口头/类比/受众分析等多个维度，而 public speaking 只是其中一种，且方向更窄。

translation.title: 2022年6月·第2套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍南京长江大桥 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 南京长江大桥是长江上首座由中国设计、采用国产材料建造的铁路、公路两用桥，上层的4车道公路桥长4589米，下层的双轨道铁路桥长6772米。铁路桥连接原来的天津一浦口和上海―南京两条铁路线，使火车过江从过去一个半小时缩短为现在的2分钟。大桥是南北交通的重要枢纽，也是南京的著名景点之一。 南京长江大桥的建成标志着中国桥梁建设的一个飞跃，大大方便了长江两岸的物资交流和人员来往，对促进经济发展和改善人民生活起到了巨大作用。
translation.reference_en:
The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge is the first road-rail bridge over the Yangtze River that was designed by China and built with domestic materials. Its upper deck, a four-lane highway, is 4,589 meters long, while its lower deck, a double-track railway, is 6,772 meters long. The railway bridge connects the two former railway lines, the Tianjin-Pukou line and the Shanghai-Nanjing line, reducing the time for trains to cross the river from one and a half hours in the past to just two minutes now. The bridge is both an important hub for north-south transportation and one of the famous tourist attractions in Nanjing. The completion of the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge marks a great leap in China’s bridge construction. It has greatly facilitated the exchange of goods and the movement of people between the two banks of the Yangtze River, and has played a huge role in promoting economic development and improving people’s lives.
【衔接】
第1句内部上下层用while对比第1句描述上下层两个长度 上层的4车道公路桥长4589米，下层的双轨道铁路桥长6772米，两者是并列对照关系，英文在两个分句间用 while 连接（the upper deck ... is 4,589 meters long, while its lower deck ... is 6,772 meters long），显出上下层的对比，比用句号硬断或 and 平接更连贯。
第3、4句用It承接避免重复桥名第3句主语「大桥」、第4句涉及「大桥的建成」，紧跟第1、2句反复出现 the bridge。为避免桥名/the bridge 一再重复，第3句主语用 The bridge 后，第4句的影响部分改用代词 It 承接（It has greatly facilitated...），指代清晰又不啰嗦。
第4句两重作用间用and并补语义第4句 大大方便了长江两岸的物资交流和人员来往 与 对促进经济发展和改善人民生活起到了巨大作用 是建成影响的两个并列方面，译文间用 and 连接两个完成时谓语，并保持时态一致，使「多重作用」读起来是顺承递进的一串，而非各自孤立。

cohesion.detail: 第1句描述上下层两个长度 上层的4车道公路桥长4589米，下层的双轨道铁路桥长6772米，两者是并列对照关系，英文在两个分句间用 while 连接（the upper deck ... is 4,589 meters long, while its lower deck ... is 6,772 meters long），显出上下层的对比，比用句号硬断或 and 平接更连贯。

cohesion.detail: 第3句主语「大桥」、第4句涉及「大桥的建成」，紧跟第1、2句反复出现 the bridge。为避免桥名/the bridge 一再重复，第3句主语用 The bridge 后，第4句的影响部分改用代词 It 承接（It has greatly facilitated...），指代清晰又不啰嗦。

cohesion.detail: 第4句 大大方便了长江两岸的物资交流和人员来往 与 对促进经济发展和改善人民生活起到了巨大作用 是建成影响的两个并列方面，译文间用 and 连接两个完成时谓语，并保持时态一致，使「多重作用」读起来是顺承递进的一串，而非各自孤立。

main_idea.core: 客观介绍南京长江大桥
main_idea.detail: 全段在客观介绍一座桥梁的概况——它的身份、长度、连接的线路、地位以及建成的意义，属于典型的「中国工程/景观介绍」客观陈述语体。开篇 南京长江大桥是长江上首座由中国设计、采用国产材料建造的铁路、公路两用桥 就是「是」字判断句，陈述这座桥客观存在的属性，奠定了全篇平实、客观的说明文基调。这类介绍文不带个人情感，用词宜简洁准确，不堆华丽辞藻。

tense.detail: 全篇主体是在客观陈述这座桥「现在仍然如此」的事实属性——它是什么桥、有多长、是什么枢纽、是著名景点，这些都是当下成立的客观状态，故主时态用一般现在时，如 大桥是南北交通的重要枢纽，也是南京的著名景点之一。只有两处需偏离：讲「建成」这一已完成的历史动作时用一般过去时（建成于过去），讲建成后「起到了巨大作用」这一从过去延续到现在的影响时可用现在完成时。

term_notes.detail: 拟定统一译法 the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge。取法：专名「南京」「长江」用约定俗成的音译/通名 Nanjing、Yangtze River，通名「大桥」意译为 Bridge，整体是国际通用的官方译名。全篇凡指这座桥，首次用全称 the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge，复现时统一用 the bridge / it 承接，绝不一会儿 Nanjing Bridge、一会儿 Yangtze Bridge 地变来变去。锚回原文：南京长江大桥。
拟定统一译法 the Tianjin-Pukou railway line。取法：两个地名「天津」「浦口」均用音译 Tianjin、Pukou，中间用连字符连接表示「这条连接两地的铁路线」，后加通名 railway line 点明性质。锚回原文：天津一浦口。
拟定统一译法 the Shanghai-Nanjing railway line。取法同上：地名音译 Shanghai、Nanjing 用连字符连接，加 railway line。注意「南京」在桥名和此处都出现，全篇统一拼 Nanjing，不可一处 Nanjing 一处 Nanking。锚回原文：上海―南京。

steps.text: 桥是首座两用桥（主系表）（主语策略：原句主语）本句中文有现成主语「南京长江大桥」，核心是「是……两用桥」这个判断，故英文主干用主系表结构：主语 the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge，系动词 is，表语 the first ... road-rail bridge。中文里 南京长江大桥是长江上首座由中国设计、采用国产材料建造的铁路、公路两用桥 的「是……桥」被提为英文主干，其余「由中国设计、采用国产材料建造」都是修饰这座桥的成分，不进主干。后半两个「长……米」是两个并列的补充说明，另作处理。

长修饰降级为过去分词定语表语 bridge 前的一长串中文修饰 由中国设计、采用国产材料建造的 不能堆在名词前，降级为过去分词短语作后置定语：designed by China and built with domestic materials，挂在 bridge 后。中文 铁路、公路两用桥 译为复合形容词 road-rail，「首座」译为 the first 放最前。后半 上层的4车道公路桥长4589米，下层的双轨道铁路桥长6772米 是对这座桥的补充描述，另起一句用 with 短语或独立句承接（the upper deck ... is ... long; the lower deck ... is ... long），避免与主干硬塞成流水句。

时态主干 is 用一般现在时，回指全篇基调——这座桥现在仍是这样一座两用桥，是客观事实。后半描述上下层长度的 is 同样用现在时。 语态「由中国设计」「采用国产材料建造」动作的承受者是桥，故用被动 designed by China、built with domestic materials；过去分词本身即被动，安放在 bridge 后作定语。 数词与单位「4589米」「6772米」译为 4,589 meters、6,772 meters，单位 meter 跟在大于一的数后用复数 meters；「4车道」译 four-lane（复合形容词中 lane 用单数）、「双轨道」译 double-track。 冠词特指这座唯一的桥用定冠词 the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge；「首座」唯一最高级语境用 the first。

The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge is the first road-rail bridge over the Yangtze River that was designed by China and built with domestic materials. Its upper deck, a four-lane highway, is 4,589 meters long, while its lower deck, a double-track railway, is 6,772 meters long.

铁路桥连接两条线（主谓宾）（主语策略：原句主语）本句主语现成——「铁路桥」the railway bridge；核心动词「连接」connects 作谓语；宾语是「两条铁路线」the two railway lines。主干即 the railway bridge connects the two railway lines。中文 铁路桥连接原来的天津一浦口和上海―南京两条铁路线 的「连接」被提为谓语，后半 使火车过江从过去一个半小时缩短为现在的2分钟 是连接带来的结果，另作降级处理。

「使……缩短」降级为分词状语后半 使火车过江从过去一个半小时缩短为现在的2分钟 是「连接」带来的结果，降级为现在分词短语作结果状语：reducing the time for trains to cross the river from one and a half hours to two minutes，挂在主干后。「原来的」译 formerly / former 修饰两条线；「从……缩短为……」用 reduce ... from ... to ... 这一固定搭配，把「过去一个半小时」「现在2分钟」分别放进 from 和 to。注意避免照中文用 and 连接「连接……并使……缩短」拼成流水句。

时态connects 用一般现在时，回指全篇基调——铁路桥现在仍发挥着连接作用，是持续事实。结果状语 reducing 用分词，时态依附主句，无需另定。 单复数「两条铁路线」是复数 the two railway lines；火车泛指多列用复数 trains；「一个半小时」one and a half hours 中 hours 用复数，「2分钟」two minutes 用复数。 介词搭配固定搭配 reduce ... from ... to ...（从……减到……）；「过江」cross the river 中 the river 特指长江用 the。 冠词特指承上文那座桥的铁路部分用 the railway bridge；特指那两条具体的线用 the two railway lines。

The railway bridge connects the two former railway lines, the Tianjin-Pukou line and the Shanghai-Nanjing line, reducing the time for trains to cross the river from one and a half hours in the past to just two minutes now.

大桥既是枢纽也是景点（主系表）（主语策略：原句主语）主语现成——「大桥」，承上文用代词或定指 the bridge / It；本句是两个并列的判断「是……枢纽」「也是……景点」，英文用主系表，谓语 is，两个并列表语用 both ... and ... 连接：both an important hub ... and one of ... attractions。中文 大桥是南北交通的重要枢纽，也是南京的著名景点之一 整句就是对桥地位的双重判断，无须切分主干之外的成分。

本句结构简单无需大改本句是简单的双重判断句，主干立好后基本无需降级处理。仅两点小重构：「南北交通的重要枢纽」译 an important hub for north-south transportation，「南北」作复合形容词 north-south；「南京的著名景点之一」用 one of + 复数 的固定结构 one of the famous tourist attractions in Nanjing。

时态is 用一般现在时，回指全篇基调——桥现在仍是枢纽和景点，客观事实。 固定结构单复数「……之一」用 one of the + 复数名词：one of the famous tourist attractions，attractions 必须用复数（之一意味着有多个）；主语 one 仍是单数，但本句系动词跟的是大桥这个主语用 is。 冠词承上指那座桥用 the bridge / It；「重要枢纽」泛指一个枢纽用不定冠词 an important hub。
The bridge is both an important hub for north-south transportation and one of the famous tourist attractions in Nanjing.

建成标志着一个飞跃（主谓宾）（主语策略：原句主语）本句主语是「南京长江大桥的建成」——一个动作名词短语 the completion of the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge；核心动词「标志着」marks 作谓语；宾语「一个飞跃」a leap。主干即 The completion ... marks a leap。中文 南京长江大桥的建成标志着中国桥梁建设的一个飞跃 是首要判断，后两个分句 大大方便了长江两岸的物资交流和人员来往 与 对促进经济发展和改善人民生活起到了巨大作用 是建成带来的两重作用，另作并列处理。

后两重作用降级为并列谓语本句一个主语带三个动作：「标志着」「方便了」「起到了作用」。主干留 marks，后两个 大大方便了长江两岸的物资交流和人员来往 译并列谓语 has greatly facilitated the exchange of goods and movement of people、对促进经济发展和改善人民生活起到了巨大作用 译 has played a huge role in promoting economic development and improving people’s lives，用 and 连接两个 has done。其中「促进经济发展」「改善人民生活」是 in 的对象，用动名词 promoting、improving。注意三个动作主语相同，不必重复主语。

时态「标志着」marks 用一般现在时（建成的意义至今成立）；「方便了」「起到了作用」是从建成那时起延续至今的影响，用现在完成时 has facilitated、has played——这是本句允许偏离基调之处，因为强调「已经并持续产生」的效果。 动名词搭配「对……起到作用」用 play a role in doing；「促进经济发展」「改善人民生活」作 in 的宾语，动词须变动名词 promoting economic development、improving people’s lives。 单复数与所有格「人员来往」movement of people、「人民生活」people’s lives 中 lives 用复数（众人各自的生活）；people’s 用所有格撇号。 主谓一致主语 the completion 是单数，故 marks 用第三人称单数 s，完成时助动词用 has 而非 have。

The completion of the Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge marks a great leap in China’s bridge construction. It has greatly facilitated the exchange of goods and the movement of people between the two banks of the Yangtze River, and has played a huge role in promoting economic development and improving people’s lives.
